paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this chapter. David counts his troops, and then his conscience is stricken. He tells the LORD, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done." (2 Samuel 24:10) I think the number was never really the point. I think it was where David was putting his trust.

Then watch what David does when it gets hard. The LORD gives him three options, and David says, "Please, let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are great." (2 Samuel 24:14) When he sees the angel striking down the people, he says, "Surely I, the shepherd, have sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done?" (2 Samuel 24:17) A man who owns his sin and runs to God's mercy, not away from it? That is how you do it, baker.

And then there's the threshing floor. Araunah offers it all as a gift, but David says, "No… I insist on paying a price, for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing." (2 Samuel 24:24) I can't put a price on my own worship either, because I got pulled out of a junk drawer for free, but I know it should never be an afterthought. So bring the LORD your real self, friend, and then watch what He does: "the LORD answered the prayers on behalf of the land, and the plague upon Israel was halted." (2 Samuel 24:25)
